claim: The FDM creativity gap (functional decomposition plus morphology gives weak creativity support, abstraction does not find the real crux, psychological inertia remains) is argued from literature and worked examples only. No controlled experiment measures the gap or the fix.
agent_test: Compare scaffold with and without a task-questioning step on the same problem set, equal tokens, blind-rated novelty. This tests the gap on the agent, which the literature never did.

claim: TRIZ-FDM integrations are hard because TRIZ needs a working principle before performance and harmful-effect problems exist, and EMS function models have no subject for SAO. The group counts 10 integration proposals and 5 issues. Both counts are second-hand from the authors' own review.
agent_test: Check which TRIZ tools an agent can run before it commits to a working principle. Ablate: contradiction step before vs after principle choice.

claim: Teaching TRIZ to humans in short courses changes the idea mix in most studies. It raises novelty or variety in several, but quantity often falls or does not change. Sizes and directions vary widely.
agent_test: Run agent ideation with a TRIZ-principles prompt vs plain prompt, score fluency, novelty and variety separately, equal tokens.

claim: Hernandez et al. (2012): novelty gain was significant at only two of three sites (p=0.0004, 0.0145; third p=0.5786). Quantity differences were not significant at any site (p=0.29, 0.54, 0.63). Authors call the effect a trend. One task, one lecture. So the headline 'TRIZ raises novelty and cuts quantity' is weaker than stated.
agent_test: Do not cite as established. Replicate on the agent with 3 separate task families and report per-family significance.

claim: Ogot and Okudan (2006): sections taught the contradiction matrix produced about twice as many feasible concepts per team (8.94 vs 4.42) in a first-year course. This conflicts in direction with Hernandez (quantity down) and Dumas 2016 (fluency down 19.3 percent).
agent_test: Count feasible concepts, not raw ideas, when comparing TRIZ and plain arms. Report both.

claim: A simple TRIZ-derived ideation prompt (Belski group) once raised idea counts, but a later study found no difference (5.03 vs 5.04 vs 4.20 distinct ideas). This is a failed replication of the gain, seen only in snippets.
agent_test: Repeat with several seeds and prompts; check whether gains survive a different task set.

claim: Students using TRIZ spend more reasoning on problem definition (function, expected behaviour) than students brainstorming. Small N (11 teams), no outcome-quality link.
agent_test: Measure the share of agent tokens spent on problem restatement under a TRIZ-style scaffold vs plain, and whether that predicts final rating.

claim: Plain LLM prompting of TRIZ is brittle. AutoTRIZ over 100 runs per case gave unstable contradiction pairs (entropy scale up to 6.64). Only 7 of 10 textbook cases matched or half-matched in the top 3. Fixing the chain in code and the matrix lookup as a table is the authors' remedy.
agent_test: Run the contradiction step 100 times at equal tokens, measure entropy, compare a code-fixed lookup vs free LLM reasoning.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: TRIZ-GPT (GPT-4): chain-of-thought gave best contradiction recall (0.691, precision 0.310) over basic (0.675/0.259). Few-shot cut recall to about 0.245. Recall rewards over-generation. On 10 post-cutoff cases recall fell to 0.544 (GPT-4) and 0.400 (GPT-3.5). Re-checked in the paper text.
agent_test: Check that exemplar prompts do not shrink the candidate set; compare recall and precision on post-cutoff cases only.

claim: In TRIZ-GPT the solution step is insensitive to prompt style: cosine similarity to documented solutions about 0.82 to 0.83 in all four strategies. Embedding similarity to a reference solution is a weak creativity measure.
agent_test: Do not use embedding similarity to a reference as a creativity score; use blind rubric or expert ratings.

claim: Detecting that a contradiction exists is easier for LLMs (F1 0.75 to 0.87) than naming the right parameter pair (pair F1 0.29 to 0.45 on cases, patent Hit@3 0.13 to 0.31). TRIZBench: 590 source documents, 734 cases with principles. Labels partly model-made.
agent_test: Split the agent's contradiction step into detect vs name, and score each separately.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: On TRIZBench principle prediction, non-LLM baselines match or beat zero-shot LLMs. Plain matrix lookup gets Hit@3 0.67 (cases) and 0.48 (patents), TF-IDF 0.69 and 0.56. Zero-shot Qwen3-8B gets 0.39 and 0.27. LLM reranking of matrix candidates reaches 0.71 and 0.59, a small gain over TF-IDF. Structure plus retrieval helps; raw LLM choice does not. AutoTRIZ already puts the lookup in code and uses the LLM only to name the pair. No test shows free LLM choice of principle beating lookup.
agent_test: Arm test: matrix lookup alone vs LLM free choice vs lookup plus LLM rerank, equal tokens, same principle labels.

claim: GPT-4 over-detects contradictions. In Trapp and Warschat (100 patents) zero-shot sentence recall was 0.71, precision 0.46, F1 0.56, with 3.19 false positives per patent. The widely quoted 0.93 is a BERTScore, not a sentence F1. GPT-4 found a contradiction in 86 of 100 patents labelled contradiction-free. Caveat from gap search: the 86 of 100 rate rests on human labels the authors themselves doubt (golf ball example), so it is an upper bound on hallucination. TRIZBench prompts with an abstain instruction still reach only HasF1 0.75 to 0.87.
agent_test: Measure the agent's false-positive rate for 'there is a contradiction' on cases that have none; add an abstain option.

claim: LLM plus TRIZ in a structured pipeline gave more ideas and more variety than TRIZ experts' textbook answers, with mixed novelty (one case expert higher) and wide quality spread. Counts favour a generator on demand; textbooks print few ideas.
agent_test: Match idea budgets between arms before comparing; rate novelty blind with two raters and report kappa.

claim: Plain GPT-3 solutions were rated more feasible and less novel than crowd human solutions. Prompt wording ('unique') and few-shot examples move diversity measurably (embedding similarity 0.746 vs 0.804).
agent_test: Test an anti-anchor instruction on the ideation step at equal tokens, measuring embedding spread.

claim: Multi-agent TRIZ with a manager and specialist agents reproduced the physical contradictions of one published case but missed six useful links and had no feedback loop. The TRIZ specialist rarely used its retrieval tool. IdeaForge convergence claims come from TinyLlama on 5 domains and are weak. Cost: 60 to 80 graph calls and 150,000 to 250,000 tokens per run. No single-agent control or token-matched comparison exists.
agent_test: Compare a single-agent TRIZ chain vs multi-role at equal tokens on the same cases, and track tool-use rate.

claim: LLM help for students using the contradiction matrix did not raise design quality overall (Cok et al. 2026, N=113, 62 with LLM and 51 without, three problems). Method main effect F(1,108)=3.21, p=.076. Only the wind turbine problem showed a gain (F(1,108)=34.67, p<.001), and that group was AI-specialised. Students found defining the contradiction easier with the LLM (d=-0.78). Cell means were not read.
agent_test: Run the scaffold with and without the contradiction step on three problems of different difficulty and rate blind. Expect a problem-by-method interaction, not a uniform gain.

claim: Semantic and NLP work on TRIZ before 2022 rarely reported benefits or limits: of 57 papers, 12 clearly did and 31 did not. Detailed TRIZ success and failure cases are seldom shared. The field lacks shared evaluation, which TRIZBench starts to fix.
agent_test: Pre-register metrics before testing TRIZ operators on the agent.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: TRIZ-based design outputs are mostly checked by authors' own metrics or one case. The AutoTRIZ battery case reports +24%, +64%, +26% over the best prior scheme from the authors' own model; no independent replication, no plain-LLM baseline arm.
agent_test: Ask for a plain-LLM baseline with the same simulation. Treat as anecdote.

claim: No source tests the 2018 Fiorineschi et al. Problem-Solution Network proposal against any control, with humans or LLMs. A search for LLM tests of their work found none.
agent_test: Implement problem-solution co-evolution (how-to question network) as a scaffold arm and run it against plain decomposition.

claim: Closest modern-model test of a TRIZ step: with Claude Sonnet 4.5 on one chair, a vanilla 'make it lighter' prompt scaled dimensions (mass -31.8%, stress +64.1%), while prompts carrying the strength-weight contradiction and a named principle gave structural changes (mass -4.0 to -14.7%, stress -0.1 to +40.7%). N=1 design, no novelty rating.
agent_test: Repeat on 10 design problems with 5 samples per arm, blind-rate structural novelty, equal tokens.

claim: No study isolates typed TRIZ proposals from untyped ones. TRIZa beat reruns of its baselines on three tasks (CICIoT2023 macro-F1 0.8325 to 0.8483) but its authors say the gain cannot be assigned to TRIZ, to the information measure, or to the workflow. AutoTRIZ has no non-TRIZ baseline either.
agent_test: Ablate: contradiction-typed mutation vs free mutation at equal token budget.

claim: TRIZ-RAGNER reports F1 84.2 vs 76.9 for GPT with prompt engineering, with each of retrieval, rerank and structured prompt worth 4 to 8 points in ablation. The paper has stray unrelated text, no sample sizes and no variance, so it is weak evidence.
agent_test: Do not rely on it. Test grounding the contradiction step in the fixed 39-parameter list.

claim: An abstain instruction does not make contradiction detection reliable. In TRIZBench every arm was told to abstain; case-level detection F1 was 0.75 to 0.87 zero/few-shot and 0.88 to 0.90 with LoRA. Few-shot examples gave small, sometimes negative, changes. No source tests abstain against no-abstain, or a second pass.
agent_test: Compare one-pass naming, naming with a none-found exit, and naming plus an independent checker on problems with and without a real contradiction.

claim: Human TRIZ studies differ in the sign of the quantity effect. Side by side, the gains come with a full course or a per-team count (Ogot, 8.94 vs 4.42 concepts) and the losses with one lecture (Hernandez n.s.; Dumas -19.3% fluency after 50 minutes). This is a pattern in the table, not a tested cause, and half the numbers are second-hand.
agent_test: For an agent training length does not exist. Test instead whether forcing the contradiction step first cuts idea count at equal tokens.

claim: Cost per run for a manager-plus-specialists TRIZ system was 150,000 to 250,000 tokens over 60 to 80 calls (one case, two runs). No paper reports tokens per novel idea or compares a single agent at the same budget, so quantity-versus-novelty cost and the multi-agent question remain untested.
agent_test: Report tokens per blind-rated novel idea for single chain, TRIZ chain and multi-agent TRIZ at matched budget.

claim: By 2026-11-19 an arXiv search for TRIZ with LLM finds 7 relevant papers. None combines blind rating by independent raters, kappa, and problems published after the model's training cutoff. LLM-TRIZ gains remain unverified on novelty.
agent_test: Build a held-out set of post-cutoff problems with two blind raters and report kappa.
